title: Coroutines and null safety
summary: Run two suspend tasks in a coroutine scope, then diagnose a forced unwrap.

scenario.briefing: A campus dashboard loads two counters concurrently. Use structured concurrency and keep nullable values explicit.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Diagnose a realistic mistake and choose the correct repair.

misconceptions.description: Launching work outside a structured coroutine scope.
misconceptions.testDescription: The work runs in a coroutine scope with two async tasks.
misconceptions.feedback: GlobalScope does not tie the work to the caller. A coroutineScope block waits for its children and cancels them with the parent.

misconceptions.description: Awaiting each task before starting the next.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Starting one async task, awaiting it, and only then starting the second.
misconceptions.feedback: Awaiting immediately serializes the work. Start both async tasks first, then await both Deferred values.
!! throws a NullPointerException when the value is absent. Use ?: or a safe call so absence is handled as data.

misconceptions.description: Assuming cancelled parents leave children alive.
misconceptions.feedback: Structured concurrency cancels children with the parent. Cleanup belongs in finally or NonCancellable.

sections.title: Kotlin functions and collections
sections.body: Functions declare parameter and return types: fun add(left: Int, right: Int): Int = left + right. listOf and mutableListOf create lists, while map transforms them. Classes and data classes compose state with behavior.

sections.title: Kotlin errors and tools
sections.body: Exceptions signal failure, and runCatching wraps a result. Coroutines use suspend functions, coroutineScope, and async for structured concurrency. Gradle builds and tests the project, the Kotlin compiler produces bytecode, and JUnit runs tests.

hints: The double bang is where the null is forced.
Do not catch the crash later; handle absence now.

statements.label: coroutineScope waits for its children before it returns.
async starts work and returns a Deferred value.
Cancelling a parent scope leaves its children running.
The !! operator is the safest way to unwrap a nullable value.

steps.explanation: Structured concurrency ties child lifetimes to their scope. Deferred values are awaited explicitly, and cancellation propagates.
